bull_bear.body: Priority on land aggregation (Lucknow focus); Debt repayment optional due to negative net debt status; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but cash-rich balance sheet supports potential payouts.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on Solano Gardens phased launches; Regulatory delays in RERA approvals for new commercial projects; Over-reliance on Lucknow market dynamics; Interest rate sensitivity (though management claims low correlation currently).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and optimistic; Emphasizes 'multi-year up-cycle' in Lucknow; Transparent about RERA cash locks and debt position; Conservative on pricing sustainability (expects stabilization vs. recent sharp CAGR).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Negative net debt is structural due to RERA norms (70% collections locked), not just excess cash; Bareilly recovery was an equity instrument with minimum guarantee, now fully unwound; Management hints at undisclosed LDA auction wins not yet in public domain.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend per share has been held steady and stepped up once: ₹8.0 in FY22, FY23 and FY24, then ₹9.0 in FY25 and FY26, against EPS of ₹51.7, ₹45.1, ₹34.4, ₹21.9 and ₹24.7 over the same years.
- The deck's stated financial pillar is "Prudent Financial Management" — a strong balance sheet and the "ability to fund business operations by taking advances from customers"; management frames the goal as "sustainable growth while maintaining balance sheet prudence".
- Full-year profitability has compressed materially even as scale grew: total income rose from ₹137.2 crore (FY22) to ₹175.7 crore (FY26), while EBITDA fell from ₹69.9 crore at a 51.0% margin to ₹41.5 crore at 23.6%, and PAT from ₹50.8 crore at 37.0% to ₹24.3 crore at 13.8%.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: promoters 55%, institutions 1%, others 44%. Market capitalisation ₹737 crore on 9.8 mn shares outstanding, with free float stated at ₹319 crore / 43% (stock price ₹750; 52-week high/low ₹1,061 / ₹690, as on 12 August 2026, source BSE).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- brand: Trusted brand built over four decades of operating history in Lucknow real estate — evidence: "Trusted brand built over four decades with a strong track record of quality and timely delivery" and 69 completed projects delivered to date.
- distribution: Government-auction land sourcing route avoids extended capital lock-in versus private land assembly — evidence: "Land for two of the three new parcels added during the year was secured through government auction, a route that avoids the extended capital lock in and price uncertainty associated with private land assembly."
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-city geographic concentration in Lucknow — EHIL's operations and project pipeline are concentrated in Lucknow and Uttar Pradesh, making performance sensitive to that single regional market's demand, pricing and regulatory environment rather than diversified across geographies.
- Dependence on the residential real estate demand cycle — The business depends on continued strength in Indian and Lucknow residential demand; the MD&A itself notes housing sales nationally 'moderated amid price inflation and macroeconomic uncertainties' during the review period.
- Execution risk across a large number of simultaneous projects — Five ongoing projects with completion dates spread out to Jun-29 require sustained construction execution, land approvals and delivery discipline across multiple sites concurrently.
- Regulatory/approval dependency — Project timelines depend on external approval processes; management notes the state's new floor area ratio and approval-timeline policy is a change that could equally have gone the other way, indicating sensitivity of the pipeline to regulatory policy shifts.
- Macroeconomic and interest-rate sensitivity — Management's own outlook flags global geopolitical tensions, elevated energy prices and moderating growth expectations, and links housing affordability and buyer sentiment to prevailing interest rates and monetary policy.
- Large multi-entity corporate structure — The Company has 42 wholly owned subsidiaries, most single-purpose real estate SPVs, adding structural and administrative complexity to group oversight and reporting.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Residential (Plots/Villas): High margin, primary growth driver (Solano); Group Housing: Lower margin, steady volume; Commercial: <10% of portfolio, opportunistic small projects (City Courtyard, Imperia Avenue).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Limited large-cap pure-play exposure to Tier-2 real estate up-cycle; Eldeco's Solano launch validates Lucknow demand. | Eldeco Housing & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of own land bank monetization and Lucknow market expansion; Negative net debt provides unique safety margin. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Four stated pillars of the EHIL story: market leadership in Lucknow (strong brand for trusted delivery; Lucknow described as the fastest-growing city with high demand for residential and township projects, and among the top Tier-2 cities for real-estate growth); execution capability across verticals; prudent financial management; and ~40 years of experience.
- Group-level (Eldeco Group, not the listed entity) credentials cited: high brand recall in North India, key player in UP since 1985, over 40 years of experience, 200 projects delivered with 32 under execution, and 30,000+ satisfied customers.
- The completed-projects annexure for EHIL lists 69 projects totalling 1,69,15,502 sq ft of saleable area, all in Lucknow, spanning townships, group housing, commercial, local shopping, plots and villas, and EWS/LIG.
- Lucknow market drivers set out by the deck: capital of UP, hub of services in Central and Eastern UP, influx of population from Eastern UP and Bihar, prominent educational institutions (IIM-L, NLU, IHM), a metro rail network and direct air connectivity with all major cities.
- Awards cited for the Eldeco Group include Top Real Estate Developer of North India at the Hurun India Real Estate Excellence Awards 2025, and earlier CWAB 2021 'India's Top Builders 2021 in the North', 'Business Leadership Awards 2021 — Developer of The Year (Residential)' and 'Stalwarts of the North Delhi NCR'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership] Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Pankaj Bajaj (25+ years, IIM Ahmedabad, President of CREDAI NCR), Group CEO Mr. Manish Jaiswal (15+ years, previously Unitech, M3M, Tribeca), EHIL COO Mr. SK Jaggi (30+ years, previously Ansal Group, Emaar MGF, Eldeco Infra) and Group VP Accounts & Taxation Mr. Rajiv Khurrana (CA and CWA, ~30 years).
- [Geographic concentration] Every ongoing, forthcoming and completed project listed in the deck is in Lucknow; the only locations named outside it (Panipat, Neemrana, Ludhiana) appear in the ESG section as Eldeco Group properties, not as EHIL projects.
- [Disclosure] Three of the four land-bank entries, including the headline 50.3-acre contracted parcel, are listed only as "Undisclosed Location 1/2/3", so the strategic location management refers to cannot be verified from the deck.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Q3 EBITDA margin 43.7% driven by high-margin Imperia Phase 2 deliveries; Sustainable long-term blended margin guided at 30-35%; Plot margins > Group Housing margins; Construction spend 9M FY26: INR 116.5 Cr.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Imperia Phase 2 to recognize ~INR 299 Cr over next 4-5 quarters; Margin: Sustainable blended EBITDA margin ~30% (near-term higher due to project mix); Order Inflow: Targeting >INR 500 Cr annually as 'new normal' post-Solano launch; Capex: Funded via internal accruals and operating cash flows.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 9M FY26 Bookings: INR 361.2 Cr (+29.1% YoY); Area Booked: 5.62 Lakh sq ft (+30% YoY); Key Pipeline: Solano Gardens (Phase 1 launched Jan '26, GDV >INR 1,000 Cr, 20 Lakh sq ft saleable); Eldeco City Courtyard (1.68 acres, 37k sq ft); Eldeco Imperia Avenue (25k sq ft); Unsold Inventory in ongoing projects approx. INR 50 Cr (excl. Imperia Ph2).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Land aggregation targeting 60 acres in near term (currently 40+ acres excluding Solano); Potential undisclosed LDA auction wins (residential); Multi-year up-cycle in Lucknow driven by infrastructure and wage growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue disciplined, patient capital allocation and balance sheet prudence while scaling booking value and collections.
- Grow the land pipeline through strategic parcel acquisitions in key Lucknow growth corridors, preferring government-auction routes over private land assembly to avoid capital lock-in and price uncertainty.
- Extend the integrated township development template (plotted development, villas and, in later phases, group housing) refined since Eldeco City to new projects such as Solano Gardens.
- Fund growth through a prudent balance of customer advances, internal accruals and debt rather than aggressive leverage.
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: During FY26, EHIL added nearly ₹2,000 crore of Gross Development Value to its pipeline by securing three strategic land parcels in Lucknow's key growth corridors — two via Lucknow Development Authority auctions and one along the Shaheed Path corridor. Five projects are under active construction: Eldeco Latitude 27 (expected completion Nov-27), Eldeco Trinity (May-28), Eldeco Hanging Gardens (Jun-28), Eldeco Skywalk (Jun-28) and Eldeco Solano Gardens (Jun-29), which was newly launched in FY26 with strong initial bookings.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Lucknow's residential demand has consistently exceeded new supply, supported by infrastructure investment (Metro phase 2, outer ring road, airport connectivity, expressway networks, defence corridor).
- Uttar Pradesh's February 2026 urban development policy liberalises floor area ratio norms and is expected to shorten project approval timelines, a change management believes benefits established, well-capitalised developers such as EHIL disproportionately.
- Premiumization is a key demand trend nationally and in Lucknow, with rising ticket sizes and stronger pricing power even as overall housing sales moderate.
- Lower interest rates and easing monetary policy are expected to improve housing affordability and support buyer sentiment for residential real estate.
- Developers with strong execution capabilities, established brands and a proven track record continue to gain customer preference in the current industry environment.
- The unsold inventory in ongoing projects plus upcoming phases of Solano Gardens form a pipeline management expects to monetise over the next five to seven years as projects move through design, approval and launch.
- Five ongoing projects (Eldeco Latitude 27, Eldeco Trinity, Eldeco Hanging Gardens, Eldeco Skywalk, Eldeco Solano Gardens) with a growing development pipeline and 69 completed projects delivered to date.
- Three strategic land parcels secured during FY26 added nearly ₹2,000 crore of Gross Development Value to the future pipeline, two via Lucknow Development Authority auctions and the third along the Shaheed Path corridor.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Eldeco has transitioned from a land-bank monetization story to a high-growth development phase with the Q4 launch of Solano Gardens (GDV >INR 1,000 Cr), driving 9M FY26 bookings past full-year FY25 levels. The company operates with negative net debt (Cash INR 178 Cr vs Debt INR 106 Cr), providing ample liquidity to fund aggressive land aggregation and construction without equity dilution.

The Company has 42 wholly owned subsidiaries, most single-purpose real estate SPVs, adding structural and administrative complexity to group oversight and reporting.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Eldeco Housing and Industries Limited (EHIL) is a real estate developer based in Uttar Pradesh, active since 1985, with its principal presence in Lucknow. The Company operates in both horizontal township development and vertical group housing, focused on the middle-income residential segment, covering construction, development, promotion and sale of townships, residential units and developed plots.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Lucknow's residential demand has consistently exceeded new supply, supported by infrastructure investment (Metro phase 2, outer ring road, airport connectivity, expressway networks, defence corridor).
- Uttar Pradesh's February 2026 urban development policy liberalises floor area ratio norms and is expected to shorten project approval timelines, a change management believes benefits established, well-capitalised developers such as EHIL disproportionately.
- Premiumization is a key demand trend nationally and in Lucknow, with rising ticket sizes and stronger pricing power even as overall housing sales moderate.
- Lower interest rates and easing monetary policy are expected to improve housing affordability and support buyer sentiment for residential real estate.
- Developers with strong execution capabilities, established brands and a proven track record continue to gain customer preference in the current industry environment.
- The unsold inventory in ongoing projects plus upcoming phases of Solano Gardens form a pipeline management expects to monetise over the next five to seven years as projects move through design, approval and launch.
- Five ongoing projects (Eldeco Latitude 27, Eldeco Trinity, Eldeco Hanging Gardens, Eldeco Skywalk, Eldeco Solano Gardens) with a growing development pipeline and 69 completed projects delivered to date.
- Three strategic land parcels secured during FY26 added nearly ₹2,000 crore of Gross Development Value to the future pipeline, two via Lucknow Development Authority auctions and the third along the Shaheed Path corridor.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q3 EBITDA margin 43.7% driven by high-margin Imperia Phase 2 deliveries; Sustainable long-term blended margin guided at 30-35%; Plot margins > Group Housing margins; Construction spend 9M FY26: INR 116.5 Cr.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on land aggregation (Lucknow focus); Debt repayment optional due to negative net debt status; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but cash-rich balance sheet supports potential payouts.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, EHIL added nearly ₹2,000 crore of Gross Development Value to its pipeline by securing three strategic land parcels in Lucknow's key growth corridors — two via Lucknow Development Authority auctions and one along the Shaheed Path corridor. Five projects are under active construction: Eldeco Latitude 27 (expected completion Nov-27), Eldeco Trinity (May-28), Eldeco Hanging Gardens (Jun-28), Eldeco Skywalk (Jun-28) and Eldeco Solano Gardens (Jun-29), which was newly launched in FY26 with strong initial bookings.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and optimistic; Emphasizes 'multi-year up-cycle' in Lucknow; Transparent about RERA cash locks and debt position; Conservative on pricing sustainability (expects stabilization vs. recent sharp CAGR).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- brand: Trusted brand built over four decades of operating history in Lucknow real estate — evidence: "Trusted brand built over four decades with a strong track record of quality and timely delivery" and 69 completed projects delivered to date.
- distribution: Government-auction land sourcing route avoids extended capital lock-in versus private land assembly — evidence: "Land for two of the three new parcels added during the year was secured through government auction, a route that avoids the extended capital lock in and price uncertainty associated with private land assembly."

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on Solano Gardens phased launches; Regulatory delays in RERA approvals for new commercial projects; Over-reliance on Lucknow market dynamics; Interest rate sensitivity (though management claims low correlation currently).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Negative net debt is structural due to RERA norms (70% collections locked), not just excess cash; Bareilly recovery was an equity instrument with minimum guarantee, now fully unwound; Management hints at undisclosed LDA auction wins not yet in public domain.

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- Continue disciplined, patient capital allocation and balance sheet prudence while scaling booking value and collections.
- Grow the land pipeline through strategic parcel acquisitions in key Lucknow growth corridors, preferring government-auction routes over private land assembly to avoid capital lock-in and price uncertainty.
- Extend the integrated township development template (plotted development, villas and, in later phases, group housing) refined since Eldeco City to new projects such as Solano Gardens.
- Fund growth through a prudent balance of customer advances, internal accruals and debt rather than aggressive leverage.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
